To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

elevated serum uric acid (SUA) levels are associated with a higher risk of death and cardiovascular hospitalizations in older adults with acute heart failure (HF), and that the association of SUA with mortality is stronger than with cardiovascular events.

the serum uric acid level is a novel and independent predictor of long-term mortality in elderly patients with HF and that an elevated serum uric acid at discharge confers additional prognostic information to established prognostic markers in this patient group.

the serum uric acid level at discharge was an independent predictor for all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) readmission in elderly patients with HF, and the prognostic value of serum uric acid at discharge was independent of the prognostic values of the serum uric level at admission and the other clinical variables.
